summary: Master behavioral finance pension decisions to mitigate biases and optimize fund performance. Join our expert-led 5-day course for pension professionals.
lede: Behavioral finance in pension fund decisions examines how cognitive biases and emotions influence investment choices and member behavior. This course is for pension trustees, investment professionals and scheme managers who need to identify bias in committee decisions and address its effects on fund processes. It covers applying Behavioral Portfolio Theory to asset allocation, using debiasing approaches in governance, and shaping member communications and default options through choice architecture.
audienceIntro: This program is essential for professionals responsible for the strategic direction, investment management, and governance of pension schemes who seek to align institutional processes with human psychological realities.
modules: Foundations of Behavioral Finance in Pension Management
Cognitive Biases and Heuristics in Investment Committees
Behavioral Portfolio Theory and Asset Allocation
Choice Architecture and Nudge Theory for Pension Schemes
Digital Transformation and Behavioral Data Analytics
Strategic Integration and the Behavioral Investment Policy
prerequisites: Participants should have a working knowledge of pension fund structures and basic investment principles. No prior training in psychology or behavioral science is required. A laptop is recommended for the choice architecture and risk profiling exercises.
